finding: Triggering a task id no worker will ever register returns HTTP 200 (false-positive success) and the run stays in PENDING_VERSION forever, past its own 10-minute TTL, with no worker ever arriving.
Cancel is a deterministic hard kill: 0/5 independent trials showed the task's own signal.aborted cleanup code ever executing. No output field populated in any trial.
A 200-event webhook burst from a non-retrying sender loses 0% of events in isolation but 86.5% when the same burst runs alongside other concurrent traffic sharing the same rate-limit window.
A real SIGKILL of the entire worker process tree mid-execution resolves the run at exactly 300.06s, matching the platform's own 300.00s claimed heartbeat-stall SLA, with no worker ever reconnecting.

Self-hosted Docker has zero CRIU checkpoint support (confirmed in docs and source). A wait.for() holds its full concurrency slot for the wait's entire duration: a 4-task batch on a concurrencyLimit=2 queue took 41.4s instead of the ~20s a checkpointed deployment would need.
5 truly concurrent triggers with the same idempotencyKey collapse to exactly 1 run and 1 execution, enforced via a Postgres unique constraint.

Exponential backoff wall-clock timing is real (10.8s actual vs 7.0s theoretical minimum for 3 forced failures), not retried back-to-back. Task-local in-memory state was found to reset between attempts in dev mode.
A wildcard concurrencyKey ('*') run holding a queue for 6s does not starve unrelated distinct-key runs on the same queue (previously-fixed regression, confirmed still fixed).
POST /replay genuinely re-executes a task (proven via a file-based execution counter) and reproduces byte-identical output for a pure/deterministic task.
A 4MB payload is cleanly rejected with HTTP 413 and a clear message, no hang, crash, or silent truncation.
